mnemonic.name: WOBBLE
mnemonic.summary: WOBBLE is a widely used memory aid for checking a marine diesel: Water, Oil, Belts, Bilges, Leaks and levels, and Exhaust. The first five letters are checked with the engine off; the E is checked once it is running.

reminder: Engines and installations differ. Follow your engine handbook, and ask a qualified marine engineer if anything you find is not normal for your engine.

checklists.title: Pre-start
checklists.subtitle: Engine off
checklists.intro: Work through these with the engine stopped and unable to start.
checklists.reviewNote: New in content 1.2 (owner request): pre/post-start checklists. Please approve the wording and action levels.

items.title: Coolant level
items.detail: Freshwater coolant at the correct level in the header tank or expansion bottle. Check it with the engine cold, and never open a hot pressure cap.

items.title: Raw-water seacock OPEN
items.detail: The cooling-water seacock is open. A keel-cooled engine may have a seacock only for its exhaust, or none at all.

items.title: Strainer clean and sealed
items.detail: The raw-water strainer is clear of weed and debris, and its lid is seated and sealed so it cannot draw in air.

items.title: Engine oil level
items.detail: Between the marks on the dipstick.

items.title: Gearbox oil level
items.detail: On the gearbox dipstick, or checked as your handbook describes.

items.title: Oil not milky or contaminated
items.detail: Milky, frothy or fuel-smelling oil means something is getting into it. Do not start the engine; get advice from a qualified engineer.

items.title: Belt condition
items.detail: Alternator and pump drive belts show no wear, cracking or fraying.

items.title: Belt tension
items.detail: Tensioned as your engine handbook specifies, checked with the engine stopped and unable to start.

items.title: Bilge dry and clean
items.detail: Under the engine and in the bilge: no standing water, oil or fuel. Any of these is a leak to trace before you start.

items.title: Fuel level
items.detail: Enough fuel for the trip with a good reserve, and the fuel valve open.

items.title: Seacocks, hoses and fittings
items.detail: No drips or weeping at seacocks, hoses, clips or fittings, and the exhaust hose undamaged.

items.title: Batteries and isolator
items.detail: Batteries in good condition, connections clean and tight, and the battery isolator set for starting.

items.title: Engine space ventilated
items.detail: The engine space and air intake are open and clear.

items.title: Propeller and lines clear
items.detail: No ropes, fenders or people in the water near the propeller, where it is safe and practicable to check.

items.title: Gear lever in neutral
items.detail: So the boat cannot move off as the engine starts.

items.title: Stop control works
items.detail: The stop control moves freely and is returned to the run position, or the stop switch works as your handbook describes.

checklists.title: Post-start
checklists.subtitle: Engine running
checklists.intro: Check these straight after starting and again once the engine is warm.
checklists.banner: Engine running: observe only. Keep clear of belts, pulleys, the shaft and other moving parts.
checklists.reviewNote: New in content 1.2 (owner request): pre/post-start checklists. Please approve the wording and action levels.

items.title: Water from the exhaust
items.detail: On a wet exhaust, cooling water comes out within a few seconds of starting. If it does not, stop the engine.

items.title: Warning lights out
items.detail: The oil pressure and charging warning lights go out once the engine is running.

items.title: Temperature normal
items.detail: Once warm, the temperature gauge or light shows normal running temperature.

items.title: No unusual noise or smoke
items.detail: No unusual noise, vibration or belt squeal, and no abnormal smoke colour from the exhaust.

items.title: Recheck for leaks
items.detail: Look again for leaks of water, oil or fuel, by eye only. Do not reach near belts, pulleys or the shaft while the engine runs.
